title: CRYPTONITE: Scalable Accelerator Design for Cryptographic Primitives and Algorithms
authors: Maheswaran, Karthikeya Sharma; Bossut, Camille; Wanna, Andy; Zhang, Qirun; Hao, Cong
metadata_source: arXiv PDF first page (2505.14657v1) + Crossref (ASAP 2025, pp. 17-24)
research_problem: Straight-line (loop-free) C code of cryptographic primitives synthesizes via HLS into large, non-scalable hardware and offers no parameterizable constructs for HLS DSE; the paper seeks correct-by-construction restructuring that enables resource/latency trade-off exploration, including across multiple co-deployed primitives.
method: Two stages: (1) an e-graph (egg) loop synthesizer using equality saturation plus data-dependence analysis (SVF) and GiNaC-based pattern abstraction to re-roll straight-line code into loops/arrays with preserved equivalence; (2) a hardware implementation explorer that enumerates loop/pragma variants and uses an analytical QoR estimator (latency cycles and DSP) to prune to a Pareto front, with Pareto points fed back for further refinement.
benchmark: Fiat Cryptography primitives (paper states 12 primitive types tested); reported: Curve25519, P521, P448, Secp256k1, P384 multiplication and square kernels.
hardware_platform: Xilinx xczu9eg-ffvb1156-2-e (ZCU102-class Zynq UltraScale+) as synthesis target
metrics: Latency (cycles), DSP/LUT/FF/BRAM utilization, Normalized Performance Index (NPI, weighted normalized latency+resource), speedup
main_result: LITERATURE_REPORTED: 'Cryptonite achieves scalable designs with up to 88.88% reduced resource usage and a 54.31% improvement in latency compared to naively synthesized designs'; single-kernel up to 2.75x speedup and 2.03x resource reduction; for a 3-kernel joint deployment DSP usage reduced ~62.21% and execution time by 27 cycles vs naive straight-line code.
limitations: Effectiveness depends on e-graph loop re-rolling; for Secp256k1 and P384 transformations increased latency due to loop-carried carry chains; QoR estimator only predicts latency and DSP analytically; no RTL/post-implementation comparison; ScaleHLS failed on several primitives.

title: Exact and Heuristic Allocation of Multi-kernel Applications to Multi-FPGA Platforms
authors: Shan, Junnan; Casu, Mario R.; Cortadella, Jordi; Lavagno, Luciano; Lazarescu, Mihai T.
metadata_source: PDF first page (UPCommons copy) + Crossref
research_problem: Choosing the number of compute units (CUs) per kernel and allocating them across multiple FPGAs to minimize the pipeline initiation interval of multi-kernel applications under per-FPGA resource and DRAM bandwidth constraints.
method: MINLP formulation minimizing alpha*II + beta*spreading subject to resource/bandwidth constraints; fast heuristic: relax to Geometric Programming (GPkit) for total CUs per kernel, branch-and-bound discretization, then greedy criticality-ordered allocation that consolidates CUs of a kernel on few FPGAs.
benchmark: AlexNet (16-bit fixed, 32-bit float), VGG16 (16-bit fixed) conv/pool/norm layers
hardware_platform: AWS F1 (8x Xilinx UltraScale+ FPGAs); optimizer on Intel Core i7-2600
metrics: Initiation interval, FPGA resource utilization (DSP/BRAM), spreading, optimizer CPU time
main_result: LITERATURE_REPORTED: GP+A obtains results comparable to the MINLP solver but is 2-3 orders of magnitude faster (0.78 s to 4.4 s vs ~1 min to several hours).
limitations: Only linear pipelines; all communication via off-chip DRAM (no on-chip/FPGA-to-FPGA links); power not considered; kernel execution time assumed to scale linearly with CUs and independent of placement; VGG kernels not fully optimized; FC layers not implemented; end-to-end on-board runs of the allocated designs are not the main reported result.

title: Fast Energy-Optimal Multi-Kernel DNN-like Application Allocation on Multi-FPGA Platforms
authors: Shan, Junnan; Lazarescu, Mihai T.; Cortadella, Jordi; Lavagno, Luciano; Casu, Mario R.
metadata_source: PDF first page (UPCommons accepted manuscript) + Crossref (vol. 41, no. 4, pp. 1186-1190, Apr. 2022)
research_problem: Finding minimum-power allocations of multi-kernel pipelined DNN-like applications on multi-FPGA platforms for a given throughput (II) constraint, fast enough to reprogram FPGAs at runtime as workloads change.
method: MINLP power model (static + dynamic, including DDR and PCIe transfer terms); heuristic H1 fixes F_min FPGAs and restricts each kernel to CU_min or CU_min+1 before MINLP; heuristic H2 exhaustively enumerates 2^K CU combinations with greedy allocation grouping kernels of similar execution time to lower frequency, picking minimum-power allocation.
benchmark: AlexNet (ALEX-16, ALEX-32), VGG-16, Transformer (TRANSFORMER-16, 1 encoder/1 decoder, 4 heads)
hardware_platform: AWS F1 (8x Xilinx UltraScale+); optimizer on Intel Core i7-6900K

title: CollectiveHLS: A Collaborative Approach to High-Level Synthesis Design Optimization
authors: Ferikoglou, Aggelos; Kakolyris, Andreas; Masouros, Dimosthenis; Soudris, Dimitrios; Xydis, Sotirios
